 Disorderly passenger arrested at Boston's Logan Airport 
 State Police say the man tried to get behind the American Airlines service counter. 
 By Nicole Garcia • 
 Published 1 hour ago • 
 Updated 1 hour ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC10 Boston 
 One of the first departures at the newly reopened Runway 27 at Boston’s Logan Airport. The runway was closed for the installation of an Engineered Material Arresting System, or EMAS. 
 A disorderly passenger was arrested Saturday evening at Boston Logan Airport after trying to go behind the service counter at an airline baggage office, according to Massachusetts State Police.
 Andrew Kipchirchir, 43, of Boston, was upset about damaged luggage and caused a scene at the American Airlines baggage office in Terminal B, police said.
